sources.title: Actual original W.4 fence CPU run

claims.statement: Discrete event probabilities lie in [0,1]; mutually exclusive exhaustive outcomes sum to 1. Two exclusive candidates cannot both have probability 0.9.
claims.scope: Finite discrete card/candidate sample space; no continuous-measure probability-zero claim.

evidence.supports: Definition, nonnegativity, normalization and [0,1] bound
Two exhaustive candidates sum to 1; 0.9+0.9=1.8 violates normalization

claims.statement: Three cat cards and one dog card with equal draw chances give P(cat)=3/4 and P(dog)=1/4.
claims.scope: One uniformly chosen card out of four; categories are disjoint.

evidence.locator: independent_cpu_checks.py card Counter/Fraction enumeration; stdout card_probability and card_denominator
evidence.supports: Independent numerator counts 3 and 1 and denominator 4

verification.details: Exact Fraction arithmetic from independently enumerated cards

claims.statement: A text decoder can assign predicted probabilities to candidate next tokens.
claims.scope: Mechanism of a standard text decoder, no capability or calibration claim about this repo.

evidence.supports: Learned linear transformation and softmax convert decoder output to predicted next-token probabilities

claims.statement: Natural log is base-e inverse exponentiation: p=e**a implies log(p)=a; real a can be fractional; negative powers give reciprocals.
claims.scope: Positive real p, real exponent a, base e; excludes complex branches.

evidence.locator: §4.2 E11–E14, E21, E25, E27–E28, E32 and positive-real paragraph after E2
evidence.supports: Base e, natural log/exponential inversion, reciprocal exponent and real powers
Python ** exponentiation and negative exponent semantics
One-argument math.log uses natural log

claims.statement: For a known correct class, -ln(p_correct) is a standard negative-log-likelihood penalty; it is nonnegative on (0,1], decreases as p increases, tends to zero at 1 and is unbounded as p approaches zero.
claims.scope: Single known correct class and finite positive probability; p=0 has no finite real-log value. This is a loss definition, not evidence of a trained model.

evidence.supports: Negative selected log-probability and exact class-index loss formula
Basis for independently derived sign, derivative and endpoint divergence
Nonnegativity and strict decrease; divergence as p→0+

claims.scope: Dimensionless natural-log penalties (nats); rounding only shown numeric values to 3 places.

evidence.supports: Natural logarithm and e constant

evidence.locator: stdout numeric_rows, e, e_inverse; code localcontext(prec=60)
evidence.supports: Independently computed 60-digit Decimal references and actual float observations
Original three outputs actually executed

verification.expected: Rounded costs 0.105, 0.693, 2.303, 1.386; e rounds 2.718, e^-1 rounds 0.368
verification.details: 60-digit Decimal.ln/exp independently recomputed; Decimal.quantize gives matching three-place displayed values; no copied lesson outputs used as numeric oracle.
verification.tolerance: Float vs Decimal absolute <1e-14 for logs; reciprocal <1e-15; rounded display ≤0.0005

claims.statement: For positive p1,p2, -ln(p1*p2)=-ln(p1)-ln(p2), allowing sums and per-position averages of log penalties.
claims.scope: Positive real factors. Algebraic identity itself does not require independent events; interpreting the factors as marginal joint probabilities does.

evidence.supports: Authoritative defining integral from which the log-product identity is independently derived
Explicit reviewer derivation for positive x,y
Three bounded arithmetic confirmations

claims.statement: When two correctness events are independent, their joint probability is the product of their marginal probabilities.
claims.scope: The stated independent two-question example. No assertion that all language-model positions are independent.

evidence.locator: Lecture 3 printed page 1, Independence of two events; printed page 2 independent fair toss example
evidence.supports: Definition P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) and no-information interpretation

claims.statement: Two independent events with p=0.5 each have joint p=0.25 and total cost about 1.386, the sum of the two individual log costs.
claims.scope: Four equally likely independent binary outcomes; total loss across two questions (sum), not their mean. Rounded 0.693 terms sum to displayed 1.386; exact terms sum to 1.3862943611198906.

evidence.locator: stdout independent_joint_probability, independent_outcome_denominator, dependent_joint_probability and product_identity
evidence.supports: Independent enumeration and contrasting dependent case establish the required condition
Joint product under independence

verification.observed: Enumeration joint 1/4 from 4 outcomes; exact float total 1.3862943611198906. Perfectly dependent comparison joint 1/2.
verification.details: Fractions supply probabilities; high precision reference checks total; product identity errors bounded independently.
verification.tolerance: Probabilities exact rational; loss identity abs <1e-14; three-place display ≤0.0005

claims.statement: Softmax transforms arbitrary finite real class scores into probabilities summing to one.
claims.scope: One specified class axis per input group; probabilities are normalized predictions, no calibration guarantee.

evidence.locator: softmax AST lines 2176–2216; formula and dim contract
evidence.supports: exp(x_i)/sum_j exp(x_j), normalization along dim

claims.statement: For single correct-class targets, default unweighted cross entropy averages selected negative log-probability costs; PyTorch takes raw logits and already handles the softmax/log conversion.
claims.scope: Class-index targets; weight=None, no ignored targets, label_smoothing=0, default reduction=mean. Other reductions, class weights and soft targets have their documented distinct contracts.

evidence.supports: Predicted unnormalized input logits and default mean; target forms and reduction

evidence.locator: CrossEntropyLoss AST lines 1200–1302, especially class-index formula and LogSoftmax+NLLLoss equivalence
evidence.supports: Correct-class negative log-softmax and averaging divisor; distinction between logits input and probability targets

claims.statement: The original math import, loop, -math.log(p), round(cost,3) and print compute and show three costs without updating parameters; math.log(0) raises ValueError. Python ** uses exponentiation.
claims.scope: Ordinary Python 3.13.5 scalar demo; round returns a rounded float for printing and does not assign back to cost.

evidence.supports: Natural-log contract and domain error
Three decimal places, returned value, ties-to-even
Integer, negative and fractional exponent syntax/semantics
Actual original demo execution

verification.details: Original fence run plus independent edge and exponent checks; no backward, optimizer or parameter update occurs.

claims.statement: Actual PyTorch softmax normalizes the class axis; default cross_entropy on raw logits matches mean correct-class NLL. Passing probabilities as predicted input computes a different loss.
claims.scope: 2 CPU float64 rows × 2 classes, class axis=1, target shape [2], correct class 0 for each, unweighted/no ignores/no smoothing; mean denominator=2. Bounded API check, not a model score.

Actually executed axis, reduction, raw-input and constant-shift cases

verification.details: Independent reference via Decimal.ln; row sums=1; per-row NLL matches; denominator 2; tolerance 1e-14 for unshifted checks, 1e-13 for shifted result; no parameter updates.

factual_accuracy.details: Every material probability/log/NLL/independence/softmax/CE and inline API claim is listed with independently inspected primary authority; positive-real/discrete/default-class-index scopes explicit.

numeric_verification.details: Actual original fence plus independent Decimal60 references, card/outcome enumeration, logarithmic identity, exponent/edge and three-place rounding checks passed.

figure_consistency.details: W.4 has zero image/SVG references and no graphical material, arrows or labels to verify. Four-card quantities and scalar log examples are fully specified in prose; W.3 figure is outside this section scope.

source_verification.details: Personally inspected actual HTTPS NIST docs, CPython v3.13.5 docs, MIT original Fall 2010 lecture PDF, Attention Is All You Need arXiv v7, and exact installed PyTorch commit originals. Primary versions, true inspection locators and snapshot hashes are preserved; locator records are navigation only.

limitations.details: This is scalar arithmetic/preparatory API teaching. No trained-model capability, calibration, new score or independent-position claim is inferred. p=0 is a nonfinite endpoint; Python rejects it. CE averaging claim is default unweighted class-index/no-ignore/no-smoothing; dependent event comparison is only a bounded condition check. No training, GPU, data/model download or engineering work was performed.
